_meta.indication: Reducing signs and symptoms of Crohn's disease and maintaining clinical response in adult patients with moderately to severely active disease who have had an inadequate response to conventional therapy.
_meta.receipt_date: Date of Submission April 30, 2007 (Response to CR letter; Original BLA submission March 1, 2006)

pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled induction trial of 6 months; CIMZIA or placebo administered SC at Weeks 0, 2, and 4 and then every four weeks to Week 24, with assessments at Weeks 6 and 26.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease (CDAI score of 220 to 450 points)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Two co-primary endpoints: clinical response (>100-point reduction in CDAI) at Week 6, and clinical response at both Weeks 6 and 26, assessed in the stratum with baseline CRP > 10 mg/L.
pivotal_trials.result: Week 6 clinical response 35% Cimzia vs 27% placebo (p<0.05); clinical response at both Weeks 6 and 26 23% vs 16% (p<0.05).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized treatment-withdrawal study: 428 Week-6 responders to open-label Cimzia 400 mg (Weeks 0, 2, 4) randomized to Cimzia or placebo every 4 weeks through Week 24.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with active Crohn's disease who were clinical responders at Week 6 to open-label Cimzia 400 mg induction.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Comparison between treatment groups of the percentage of patients in clinical response at Week 26, assessed in the stratum with baseline CRP > 10 mg/L.
pivotal_trials.n: 428 Week-6 responders randomized (Placebo N=210; Cimzia 400 mg N=215)
pivotal_trials.result: Week 26 clinical response 63% Cimzia vs 36% placebo (p<0.05); clinical remission 48% vs 29% (p<0.05).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5% and higher than placebo): upper respiratory infection (20% Cimzia vs 13% placebo), urinary tract infection (7% vs 6%), and arthralgia (6% vs 4%). Serious infections occurred in 3% of Cimzia vs 1% placebo; serious adverse reactions 10% Cimzia vs 9% placebo. Serious risks include tuberculosis, invasive fungal and other opportunistic infections, and malignancies/lymphoma.
target_moa: Certolizumab pegol is a TNF blocker; it binds to human TNF-alpha (KD 90 pM) and selectively neutralizes TNF-alpha, a key pro-inflammatory cytokine, without neutralizing lymphotoxin alpha (TNF-beta).
modality: PEGylated antibody Fab' fragment (recombinant, humanized Fab' conjugated to ~40 kDa polyethylene glycol; lacks an Fc region)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: RISK OF SERIOUS INFECTIONS. Tuberculosis (TB), invasive fungal, and other opportunistic infections, some fatal, have occurred. Perform test for latent TB; if positive, start treatment for TB prior to starting CIMZIA; monitor all patients for active TB during treatment.

rems.type: A REMS was approved consisting of a Medication Guide and a timetable for submission of REMS assessments.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because Cimzia is a member of the TNF-blocker class and the data posed no unique concerns.

summary.text: CIMZIA (certolizumab pegol) received a standard (traditional) review BLA originally submitted February 28, 2006; a Complete Response letter was issued December 21, 2006, and following the sponsor's resubmission the BLA was approved April 22, 2008 for Crohn's disease, with a REMS (Medication Guide) and multiple required postmarketing clinical trials/study.

citations.quote: BLA STN 125160 was originally submitted on February 28, 2006 and was granted a standard review. A complete response (CR) letter was issued on December 21, 2006. On April 30, 2007, the sponsor submitted a complete response for review.

CIMZIA™ is indicated for reducing the signs and symptoms of Crohn's disease and maintaining clinical response in adult patients with moderately to severely active disease who have had an inadequate response to conventional therapy.

Your proposed REMS is approved. The REMS consists of the Medication Guide included with this letter and the timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS included in your April 16, 2008 submission.

requirement.text: A long-term observational study in the U.S. including approximately 2000 CIMZIA-treated Crohn's disease patients and 2000 matched controls receiving other treatments, monitored for ten years.

citations.quote: 2. A long-term observational study in the U.S. that will include approximately 2000 CIMZIA™-treated Crohn's disease patients and 2000 matched controls receiving other treatments for Crohn's disease. Patients will be monitored for ten years.

requirement.text: CDP870-033, an ongoing open-label trial to assess long-term safety in patients who previously completed CDP870-031 or CDP870-032, with patient follow-up extended to seven years from start of treatment.

citations.quote: 3. CDP870-033, an ongoing open-label trial to assess the long-term safety of CIMZIA™ in patients with Crohn's disease who have previously completed trials CDP870-031 or

CDP870-032. The objectives of this trial include measurement of pharmacokinetics and antibody response in CIMZIA™-treated patients. Patient follow-up will be extended to seven years from the start of treatment.

requirement.text: CDP870-034, an ongoing open-label trial to assess long-term safety of re-exposure to CIMZIA in patients previously withdrawn from CDP870-031 or CDP870-032 due to Crohn's exacerbation, with follow-up extended to seven years from start of treatment.

citations.quote: 4. CDP870-034, an ongoing open-label trial to assess the long-term safety of re-exposure to CIMZIA™ after a variable interval in patients with Crohn's disease who were previously withdrawn from completed trials CDP870-031 or CDP870-032 due to an exacerbation of Crohn's disease. The objectives of this trial include measurement of pharmacokinetics and antibody response in CIMZIA™-treated patients. Patient follow-up will be extended to seven years from the start of treatment.

requirement.text: CDP870-088, an open-label trial to assess long-term safety in patients who completed or were withdrawn from CDP870-085, with follow-up extended to five years from start of treatment.

citations.quote: 5. CDP870-088, an open-label trial to assess the long-term safety of CIMZIA™ in patients with Crohn's disease who have either completed trial CDP870-085 or were withdrawn from CDP870-085 due to an exacerbation of Crohn's disease. The objectives of this trial include measurement of pharmacokinetics and antibody response in CIMZIA™-treated patients. Patient follow-up will be extended to five years from the start of treatment.

requirement.text: A placebo-controlled trial to assess effects of CIMZIA on antibody responses to B cell-mediated (pneumococcal) and T cell-mediated (influenza) immunization in approximately 100 placebo- and 100 CIMZIA-treated patients with active rheumatoid arthritis.

citations.quote: 6. A placebo-controlled trial designed to assess the effects of CIMZIA™ treatment on antibody responses to a B cell-mediated immunization, using pneumococcal vaccine immunization, and to a T cell-mediated immunization, using influenza vaccine, in patients with active rheumatoid arthritis. The study will measure both antibody titers and rates of clinical response in approximately 100 placebo- and 100 CIMZIA™-treated patients who will be given polyvalent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine and influenza vaccine.
A complete response (CR) letter was issued on December 21, 2006.

basis.text: FDA clinical and statistical reviewers recommended a complete response at the end of the first cycle, citing that more statistically robust induction data were warranted; Study CDP870-031 showed a small treatment effect not statistically robust in the true intent-to-treat population. (Two CMC issues were also raised in the original CR letter.)

citations.quote: Both the FDA clinical and statistical reviewers recommended a complete response be sent to the applicant based upon their review of these data at the end of the first review cycle.

- Study CDP870-031 showed a small treatment effect that is not statistically robust when clinical response is assessed for the true intent-to-treat population (i.e., all patients randomized with a baseline CRP \ge 10 mg/L) and patients with missing information are counted as non-responders.
